rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the baseline effectiveness of a multimodal (RNA + image) multiprofile setup with scgpt and imagenet_vit_l encoders, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It isolates the impact of multimodal integration and advanced encoders, which are critical design choices with high uncertainty. This provides foundational insights before exploring more complex variations.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.542 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged. It isolates the effect of image encoder choice, a critical design decision, to determine if resnet50 improves performance compared to imagenet_vit_l. This addresses uncertainty about image encoder effectiveness without changing multiple parameters.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.5419 accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping image encoder and fusion method the same isolates the effect of aggregation. It is the best next step as it focuses on a key design decision (aggregation) with minimal parameter changes, potentially revealing if transformer aggregation improves performance.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200 while keeping other settings identical, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. This directly addresses uncertainty about whether the RNA encoder significantly affects performance, a critical design decision.

Existing evidence shows config_026 (scvi_n200, ViT-L, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests transformer aggregation with the same RNA/image encoders, isolating its impact. It balances exploitation (building on top performer) and exploration (testing aggregation method), which is critical for understanding performance drivers.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_027) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l → resnet50) while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion consistent isolates the impact of image encoder choice. It directly compares two key design decisions (image encoder) with minimal changes, leveraging strong prior evidence to explore a promising direction.

Existing evidence shows that config_027 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. However, uncertainty remains about whether using resnet50 image encoder with scvi_n200 RNA (as in config_038) could yield better performance. This experiment tests the impact of swapping the image encoder (resnet50 vs imagenet_vit_l) while keeping RNA encoder and aggregation method consistent, isolating the effect of image encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the top-performing RNA encoder with exploration of alternative image encoders.

Existing evidence shows that config_027 (scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping RNA, image, and aggregation the same) impacts performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. This is critical for understanding if weighted fusion is essential for top performance, balancing exploitation of current strong evidence with exploration of key design choices.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder (both different from top-performing components) could yield better performance, isolating the impact of encoder choices while maintaining transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. It balances exploration of critical design choices with a logical extension of high-performing configurations.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l RNA/image encoders with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieve high performance. This experiment tests the impact of switching to resnet50 image encoder and singleprofile setting while keeping scvi_n200 and weighted fusion, isolating the effect of image encoder and profile setting changes. It balances exploration of key design choices with minimal prior evidence on their impact.
